title: Teaching Longitudinal Linear Mixed Models End-To-End: A Reproducible Case Study in Mouse Body-Weight Growth
extended_summary:
This paper presents a reproducible teaching case study on longitudinal linear mixed models using mouse body-weight data. The core problem is pedagogical: many learners encounter mixed models as fragmented theory or software output, so the author aims to provide a coherent end-to-end workflow that links raw data, exploratory plots, model specification, estimation, diagnostics, and interpretation.

The approach uses a preclinical mouse experiment in which 31 mice from three groups were weighed weekly over 12 weeks: wild-type controls, pair-fed ob/ob mice, and unrestricted ob/ob mice. The dataset is reshaped from wide to long format and analyzed with random-intercept linear mixed models in R. Three candidate mean structures are compared by maximum likelihood, and linear contrasts are used to estimate group differences in weekly weight trajectories and 12-week gain.

The paper is aimed at advanced undergraduate and graduate students in biostatistics, epidemiology, applied statistics, and public health methods. It reports that the unrestricted ob/ob group has a much steeper growth trajectory than the other groups, while wild-type and pair-fed mice have similar slopes. The author concludes that the case study is a useful reusable teaching module for demonstrating transparent longitudinal modeling and reproducible statistical practice.
